# dsm_firewall_rule (Data Source)

Read-only data source for looking up one rule in a Synology DSM firewall profile.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dsm_firewall_rule" "s3_from_vpn" {
  profile = "default"
  adapter = "eth0"
  name    = "S3 and HTTPS from the VPN only"
}

# A rule only enforces anything when the firewall is on and its profile is the
# active one, so both are exposed for assertions.
output "s3_rule_is_enforced" {
  value = data.dsm_firewall_rule.s3_from_vpn.firewall_enabled && data.dsm_firewall_rule.s3_from_vpn.profile_active
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `adapter` (String) Network interface the rule applies to, or `global` for every interface.
- `name` (String) Rule name, shown as Description in the DSM UI.
- `profile` (String) Firewall profile the rule belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `action` (String) What happens to matching traffic: allow or deny.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is active.
- `firewall_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the DSM firewall is switched on at all. A rule in a profile has no effect while this is false.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier: profile:adapter:name.
- `ports` (List of String) Destination ports or ranges. Null when the rule matches every port, or when it selects ports through a DSM service preset this provider does not model.
- `priority` (Number) Zero-based position of the rule in its adapter's list. Lower numbers are evaluated first.
- `profile_active` (Boolean) Whether this profile is the one currently in force. Rules in a standby profile are stored but not enforced.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol the rule matches: tcp, udp, icmp, or all.
- `source` (List of String) Source addresses. Null when the rule matches any source, or when it selects sources by GeoIP country, which this provider does not model.
